From e27b1636e9337d1a1d174b191e53d0f86421a822 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2020 11:00:01 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] genirq/PM: Always unlock IRQ descriptor in rearm_wake_irq()

rearm_wake_irq() does not unlock the irq descriptor if the interrupt
is not suspended or if wakeup is not enabled on it.

Restucture the exit conditions so the unlock is always ensured.

Fixes: 3a79bc63d9075 ("PCI: irq: Introduce rearm_wake_irq()")
Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Acked-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200811180001.80203-1-linux@roeck-us.net

diff --git a/kernel/irq/pm.c b/kernel/irq/pm.c
index 8f557fa1f4fe..c6c7e187ae74 100644
--- a/kernel/irq/pm.c
+++ b/kernel/irq/pm.c
@@ -185,14 +185,18 @@ void rearm_wake_irq(unsigned int irq)
 	unsigned long flags;
 	struct irq_desc *desc = irq_get_desc_buslock(irq, &flags, IRQ_GET_DESC_CHECK_GLOBAL);
 
-	if (!desc || !(desc->istate & IRQS_SUSPENDED) ||
-	    !irqd_is_wakeup_set(&desc->irq_data))
+	if (!desc)
 		return;
 
+	if (!(desc->istate & IRQS_SUSPENDED) ||
+	    !irqd_is_wakeup_set(&desc->irq_data))
+		goto unlock;
+
 	desc->istate &= ~IRQS_SUSPENDED;
 	irqd_set(&desc->irq_data, IRQD_WAKEUP_ARMED);
 	__enable_irq(desc);
 
+unlock:
 	irq_put_desc_busunlock(desc, flags);
 }
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `kernel/irq/pm.c`**
- The function `rearm_wake_irq()` has been modified to ensure that the IRQ descriptor is always unlocked, regardless of whether the interrupt is suspended or if wakeup is enabled.
- The exit conditions have been restructured:
  - The check for a valid `desc` is now performed first, and if it is invalid, the function returns immediately.
  - If the `desc` is valid but the interrupt is not suspended or wakeup is not set, the code now jumps to the `unlock` label to ensure the descriptor is unlocked.
  - The previous logic that allowed the function to exit without unlocking the descriptor in certain conditions has been removed.

### Relationships
- The changes made in `kernel/irq/pm.c` directly address a bug related to the handling of IRQ descriptors in the `rearm_wake_irq()` function. The restructuring of the exit conditions ensures that the descriptor is always unlocked, which prevents potential deadlocks or resource leaks when the function is called under various conditions. This modification is a fix for the issue introduced in a previous commit (3a79bc63d9075) that added the `rearm_wake_irq()` function.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c

    !irqd_is_wakeup_set(&desc->irq_data))
```
Reason:
The condition checks if the IRQ descriptor is either not present or if the interrupt is not suspended or if wakeup is not enabled. If any of these conditions are true, the function exits without unlocking the IRQ descriptor, which can lead to deadlocks or resource leaks.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (!(desc->istate & IRQS_SUSPENDED) ||
    !irqd_is_wakeup_set(&desc->irq_data))
    goto unlock;
```
Reason:
This restructuring ensures that regardless of whether the interrupt is suspended or wakeup is enabled, the function will always reach the `unlock` label, which guarantees that the IRQ descriptor is unlocked before the function exits, thus preventing potential deadlocks or resource leaks.
